transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I've been struggling with really distressing, intrusive thoughts and repetitive worries that I just can't seem to shake off. I find myself constantly doubting my own actions and worrying about things like germs and contamination. It's becoming really overwhelming to deal with every day.
When you have these intrusive thoughts about germs, do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or rituals to reduce your anxiety, like washing your hands repeatedly?

I definitely get those intense thoughts about germs and being contaminated all the time. But to be honest, I'm not really sure if I do specific rituals or repetitive hand-washing to cope with them, as I haven't really thought about it that way.
Do you ever feel a strong urge to repeat actions, like checking, counting, or cleaning, even if you don’t fully understand why—just to feel less anxious or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, I feel those strong urges constantly, especially when it comes to checking things like door locks or gas valves because I always doubt if I actually did it. I also feel compelled to wash and clean things repeatedly because of my intense fear of germs and contamination. Doing these repetitive actions is really the only way I can get some relief from the anxiety.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder", "Generalized Anxiety Disorder"], but Generalized Anxiety Disorder is now ruled out because the patient endorses clear obsessions (intrusive thoughts about germs and contamination) and compulsions (repetitive checking, washing, cleaning) that are time-consuming and performed to reduce anxiety, which is characteristic of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The symptoms go beyond generalized worry and involve specific ritualized behaviors, making OCD the most fitting diagnosis.
